team-size.transcript: How many enablement people does your sales plan need? Here is a rule of thumb. One enablement person for every 25 to 50 quota-carrying reps. Count your reps. Divide by 50, then by 25. That is the range your plan assumes. Now count the people you actually have. If the plan assumes six and you have two, the gap does not disappear. It shows up somewhere else. A kickoff with no follow-up, a launch that reps learn from a slide deck, new hires who ramp by shadowing whoever has time. The gap is not a judgment of the team. It is a planning error. The work was sized, the hours were not. Put both numbers on one page before the plan is final. Run yours in the free capacity calculator at enablement.works

four-levels.transcript: Most enablement reports stop at activity. Completion rates, logins, content views. A CRO cannot fund a plan on that. There are four levels of evidence. Activity. Did reps complete the program? Practice. Can they do it in a role play or a certification? Behavior. Do they do it on real calls? Outcome. Did ramp time, stage conversion or win rate move? Set the baseline before the program. Not after. Where you can start one team 30 days before another and compare them. One page once a month with all four levels. That is a report a CRO reads. Which level does your reporting reach today? The full guide is at enablement.works

kickoff-90-days.transcript: Every January sales teams spend heavily on a kickoff. Then February starts. The kickoff gets the budget. The 90 days after it get almost nothing. That is where the money is won or lost. Here is what those 90 days need. A short certification on the core message in the first two weeks. One roleplay per new play scored with the same scorecard managers use. Nudges to reps who have not started and a list for every manager. And a report to the CRO at day 30, 60 and 90. Who completed, who practiced and what changed on calls. None of this is hard. It takes the hours most teams spend building the kickoff itself. So who owns the 90 days after yours? The full plan is at enablement.works
